newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Explorers Index posts second sharp fall.
newsitem.headline: Australian Explorers Index posts second sharp fall.

text.p: Perth stockbroker Eyres Reed Ltd said its Australian Explorers Index fell sharply for the second consecutive week, with a fall of 78.6 points or 2.39 percent.
The All Ordinaries Index rose 2.10 percent. Changes, in percent:
Jun 13 June 6 pct 1 Month pct 1 Year pct
NOTE: The explorers index (base 500, March 1992) tracks the performance of 88 small capitalisation exploration companies.
Falls outnumbered gains three to one in the week, which followed a 1.72 percent fall the previous week.

"A shortened trading week, tax selling, mixed base metal and precious metal prices and a greater focus on heavyweight stocks all contributed to the fall," Eyres Reed analyst Glen Colgan said in a commentary.

Bendigo Gold continued its strong run, rising 10 cents to 33 cents while fellow Victorian gold hopeful Central Victorian Gold rose 2.3 cents to 11 cents after placing 5.3 million shares at 10 cents with a free attaching 1999 option.
Western Minerals rose two cents to 12 cents after being bid for by the Vancouver listed West African Gold Corporation.
Other gains included Coplex Resoures, up 6.5 cents to 45.5 cents, Metex Resources lifting three cents to 25.5 cents and Marymia Exploration which rose three cents to 28 cents.
Falls included Border Gold NL, down four cents to 24 cents as work continued on their Karonie prospects. Helix Resources lost 27 cents to A$1.38, while Yardarino Mining lost 3.5 cents to 14 cents.
Vietnam oil play Anzoil dropped 1.5 cents to six cents and Longreach Gold fell four cents to 12 cents.
